The present revision petition has been preferred by the revisionist under Section 397/399 of Code of Criminal Procedure ((hereinafter referred to as 'Cr.PC') against the order dated 22.12.2021 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Impugned Order') passed by Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court, West District, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi (herein after referred to as the 'Ld. Trial Court') in case FIR No. 1117/2014 under Section 498A/406/34/323/509 of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC') whereby charge under Section 498A/406/323/34 was directed to be framed against the present revisionists.

Arguments addressed by revisionist 2. Assailing the impugned order, revisionist submitted that the impugned order is based bad in law and contrary to the facts of the case; that the petitioners are victim of malicious prosecution by the complainant in connivance with police officials; that the Giraj Singh @ Giri Raj Singh & Ors. Vs. he State (Govt. Of NCT of Delhi) & Anr. complainant/respondent No. 2 has not made any specific allegations with dates of dowry demanded by the revisionists, hence, they cannot be prosecuted for the offence under Section 498A Cr.PC; that the complainant/respondent No. 2 was residing separately from her in- laws and they had no concern in her married life.

sentences.text: Further, there is no specific allegation of entrustment of the dowry articles to the revisionists, hence, the question of their return and misappropriation by them does not arise for constituting offence under section 406 IPC.

Further, there is no specific allegations with dates of beating by the present revisionists, hence,
no offence under Section 323 IPC is made out.
Therefore, all the revisionists deserve to be discharged in the present matter as the charge cannot be framed on vague and bald allegations without any prima facie evidence against them.
Arguments addressed on behalf of State as well as respondent No. 2 (Complainant).

3. Per contra, Ld. Addl. PP for the State supporting the Impugned Order argued that there is no infirmity and illegality done by the Ld. Trial Court and has rightly passed the order on charge and framed charges against the accused persons under the relevant sections, hence, no interference of this Court is required.

It has also been argued that the order on charge is a detailed one mentioning the specific role of the revisionist and since it is a matrimonial dispute, there is no requirement of chronological sequence of events being a continuous offence.

It has also been argued by Ld. Counsel for respondent No. 2/Complainant that the premises where the revisionists Giraj Singh @ Giri Raj Singh & Ors. Vs. he State (Govt. Of NCT of Delhi) & Anr. and respondent No. 2 reside are common and the entry / exit gate is also common for all.

sentences.text: Section 227 and 228 Cr. PC empowers a Judge to frame charge or discharge accused for the offence.

Before proceedings further, this Court deems it appropriate to reproduce both sections,
which reads as under:
"227. Discharge.
If, upon consideration of the record of the case and the documents submitted therewith, and after hearing the submissions of the accused and the prosecution in this behalf, the Judge considers that there is not sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused, he shall discharge the accused and record his reasons for so doing."
228. Framing of charge.

(1) If, after such consideration and hearing as aforesaid, the Judge is of opinion that there is ground for presuming that the accused has committed an offence which-(a) is not exclusively triable by the Court of Session, he may, frame a charge against the accused and, by order, transfer the case for trial to the Chief Giraj Singh @ Giri Raj Singh & Ors. On consideration of the authorities about scope of Sections 227 and228 of the Code, the following principles emerge:

However, at this stage, there cannot be a roving enquiry into the pros and cons of the matter and weigh the evidence as if he was conducting a trial.

(iv) If on the basis of the material on record, the Court could form an opinion that the accused might have committed offence, it can frame the charge, though for conviction the conclusion is required to be proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused has committed the offence.

The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."

Perusal of the complaint shows that there is no specific allegation of demand of dowry as no date or article or cash demanded has been mentioned by the complainant, except at one point where the complainant has stated that she was left at her parental house with directions not to return without Rs.5 Lacs.

However, as per record, husband of the complainant filed a petition under Section 9 of the Giraj Singh @ Giri Raj Singh & Ors. Vs. he State (Govt. Of NCT of Delhi) & Anr. Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for restitution of conjugal rights, which was withdrawn on settlement that they want divorce by mutual consent.

Further, mere bald allegations of demand of dowry do not justify framing of charges of such serious nature.

11. Reliance is also placed upon by this Court on the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Safia Bano Vs. The State of UP & Ors., wherein it has been observed that " However, insofar as the present appellants are concerned apart from the general and bald allegations, there is not even a whisper as to how the ingredients to constitute an offence under Section 498A of IPC made out against the present appellants."

sentences.text: Perusal of the allegations appearing against the petitioner do not show that the articles of istridhan were even entrusted to her.
In the absence of the allegation of entrustment, question of misappropriation or conversion to her use does not arise.
Thus the most vital ingredient to constitute the offence under Section 406 IPC is missing.
In view of the above, no case Section 406 IPC is spelt out against the petitioner.
7. Now coming to the offence under Section 498A IPC.
After her marriage complainant-respondent no. 2 started living with her husband who was never posted in Delhi.
Admittedly petitioner was employed in Ministry of Finance at the time of marriage of the complainant.
The petitioner was married in 1997 and since then she is living in her own matrimonial home.

Allegation made by the complainant that her husband used to misbehave with her, at the behest of the petitioner are totally vague,
inherently improbable and unworthy of credence.
From these allegation even a strong suspicion cannot be inferred.
Even the statements recorded during investigation do not furnish the requisite material so as to make out the prima facie case under Section 498A IPC against the petitioner.

8. It has almost become a practice that whenever a police report is lodged consequent upon a matrimonial discord, there is always a tendency on the part of the complainant to involve practically all the relations of her in-laws' family either out of vengeance or to curl out appropriate settlement.
Such a tendency ought to be deprecated.

b. In Onkar Nath Mishra & Ors vs State (Nct Of Delhi) & Anr reported in 2008 (2)

sentences.text: It is manifestly clear from the afore- extracted complaint as also the relevant portion of the charge- sheet that there is neither any allegation of entrustment of any kind of property by the complainant to the appellants nor its misappropriation by them.
Furthermore, it is also noted in the charge-sheet itself that the complainant had refused to take articles back when this offer was made to her by the Investigating Officer.
Therefore, in our opinion, the very pre- requisite of entrustment of the property and its misappropriation by the appellants are lacking in the instant case.

We have no hesitation in holding that the learned Additional Sessions Judge and the High Court erred in law in coming to the conclusion that a case for framing of charge under Section 406 IPC was made out."

Further, there is no specific allegations of beatings on some specific dates with specific role of revisionists.
Surprisingly, there is no supplementary statement of the complainant recorded under Section 161 Cr. PC during investigation for giving details of the alleged incidents/offence.

Therefore,
from the record, it has been surfaced that merely stereo typed allegations of harassment, beating and demand of dowry by the revisionist, who are family members of the husband of respondent No.
2 , have been made in the complaint.
The husband of the complainant has not preferred revision and proceedings against him are going on separately.

With this background and applying the ratio laid down by the Superior Courts to the present case, this Court finds that there is no prima facie is available on record against the present revisionists to frame charge under Section 498A/406/323/34 IPC against them.
Accordingly, the impunged order on charge dated 22.12.2021, is set aside.
Revisionists stand discharged for the offences for which they were charged.
15. The trial Court record along with the copy of this order be sent back to the learned Trial Court.
16. The file of this revision petition be consigned to record room after due compliance.

4 harassed her mentally and threatened her of terminating her pregnancy'.
The allegations are therefore general and omnibus and can at best be said to have been made out on account of small skirmishes.
However, as per record, husband of the complainant filed a petition under Section 9 of the Giraj Singh @ Giri Raj Singh & Ors. Vs. he State (Govt. Of NCT of Delhi) & Anr. Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for restitution of conjugal rights, which was withdrawn on settlement that they want divorce by mutual consent.
Therefore, the allegation that she was left at her parental house with condition to return with dowry does not hold any water, in view of the petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 filed by the husband himself.
Further, mere bald allegations of demand of dowry do not justify framing of charges of such serious nature.
8. It has almost become a practice that whenever a police report is lodged consequent upon a matrimonial discord, there is always a tendency on the part of the complainant to involve practically all the relations of her in-laws' family either out of vengeance or to curl out appropriate settlement.
Such a tendency ought to be deprecated.
The husband of the complainant has not preferred revision and proceedings against him are going on separately.
Giraj Singh @ Giri Raj Singh & Ors.
